# Building a 188 x 282 pooling matrix

## 1 Purpose

This vignette works through a single concrete Polynomial Pools (PP)
design: **282 specimens tested using 188 pools**, where every specimen
is placed in exactly 4 pools and every pool holds exactly 6 specimens.
That is a design with

- \\N = 282\\ specimens (columns of \\\mathbf{M}\\),
- \\J = 188\\ pools (rows of \\\mathbf{M}\\),
- pool size \\n_j = 6\\ for every pool \\j\\,
- column weight \\w_i = 4\\ for every specimen \\i\\.

## 2 Installation

`ppgt` is not yet on CRAN. Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("myaseen208/ppgt")

# or with remotes
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("myaseen208/ppgt")
```

## 3 Construction

The matrix is built with a single call to
[`pp_matrix()`](https://myaseen208.github.io/ppgt/reference/pp_matrix.md):

``` r
M4 <- pp_matrix(q = 47, d = 3, nl = 4, N = 282)
dim(M4)
  [1] 188 282
```

[`pp_matrix()`](https://myaseen208.github.io/ppgt/reference/pp_matrix.md)
builds its design over the finite field \\\mathrm{GF}(q)\\, using
dimension `d` and `nl` layers (see
[`?pp_matrix`](https://myaseen208.github.io/ppgt/reference/pp_matrix.md)
and the `ppgt_pp` vignette for the full construction). The three
arguments interact as follows:

- `q = 47` is the field order. 47 is prime, so \\\mathrm{GF}(47)\\
  exists, and each layer of the design contributes exactly \\q = 47\\
  pools.
- `nl = 4` is the number of layers, so the pool count is \\J = n_l \\ q
  = 4 \times 47 = 188\\, and every specimen is assigned to exactly \\n_l
  = 4\\ pools (one per layer).
- `d = 3` is the PP dimension, which fixes the canonical pool size to
  \\q^{d-1} = 47^2 = 2209\\ in the *full* (untruncated) design with
  \\N\_{\max} = q^d = 47^3\\ specimens.
- `N = 282` truncates that full design down to its first 282 columns.
  Because \\282 = 6 \times 47 = 6q\\ is a small multiple of \\q\\, the
  truncated design keeps only 6 of the \\q^{d-2} = 47\\ possible “column
  blocks” per pool, so every pool’s row sum drops from the full-design
  value of 2209 down to 6.

The two products \\188 = 4 \times 47\\ and \\282 = 6 \times 47\\ both
factor through \\q = 47\\, and this is exactly what keeps every row sum
equal to 6 and every column weight equal to 4 (rather than only
approximately so): \\q\\ divides \\N\\ exactly
([`pp_matrix()`](https://myaseen208.github.io/ppgt/reference/pp_matrix.md)
requires `N %% q == 0`), so the truncation boundary falls cleanly
between pool blocks and does not cut any pool’s row in half.

Every incidence \\M\_{ji} = 1\\ is counted once from the pool side (as a
1 in row \\j\\) and once from the specimen side (as a 1 in column
\\i\\), so the total number of incidences can be computed two ways: \\ J
\\ n_j = 188 \times 6 = 1128, \qquad N \\ w_i = 282 \times 4 = 1128. \\
Both give the same total, 1128, which is confirmed numerically below.

## 4 Verification

``` r
dim(M4)
  [1] 188 282

# apply() works directly on the sparse matrix, matching the original script
table(apply(M4, 1, sum))
  
    6 
  188
table(apply(M4, 2, sum))
  
    4 
  282

# rowSums()/colSums() dispatch to Matrix's sparse-aware methods (library(Matrix)
# was attached above) and are much faster for larger matrices
table(rowSums(M4))
  
    6 
  188
table(colSums(M4))
  
    4 
  282

stopifnot(
  nrow(M4) == 188L,
  ncol(M4) == 282L,
  all(Matrix::rowSums(M4) == 6L),
  all(Matrix::colSums(M4) == 4L)
)

total_incidences <- sum(M4)
total_incidences
  [1] 1128
stopifnot(total_incidences == 188L * 6L, total_incidences == 282L * 4L)
```

### 4.1 Pairwise overlap between specimens

The PP construction guarantees that any two distinct specimens share at
most \\d - 1\\ pools. With \\d = 3\\ here, that bound is 2. The
specimen-by-specimen overlap matrix is \\\mathbf{M}^\top\mathbf{M}\\;
its off-diagonal entries are the pairwise pool-sharing counts
\\\|\mathcal{J}\_i \cap \mathcal{J}\_{i'}\|\\:

``` r
overlap <- Matrix::crossprod(M4)
diag(overlap) <- 0L  # ignore the diagonal (each specimen "overlaps" itself)

max_overlap <- max(overlap)
max_overlap
  [1] 1

stopifnot(max_overlap <= 2L)  # the d - 1 = 2 theoretical bound
```

The maximum pairwise overlap actually attained, 1, is within the
theoretical bound \\d - 1 = 2\\.

## 5 Efficiency

Testing all 282 specimens individually would need 282 tests. This design
needs only \\J = 188\\ pooled tests, a saving of

``` r
n_specimens <- ncol(M4)
n_pools <- nrow(M4)

n_specimens
  [1] 282
n_pools
  [1] 188

saving_pct <- 100 * (1 - n_pools / n_specimens)
round(saving_pct, 1)
  [1] 33.3
```

so pooling 282 specimens into 188 pools cuts the number of tests by
about 33.3%, at the cost of the resolution limits discussed next.

## 6 Decoding

[`pp_decode()`](https://myaseen208.github.io/ppgt/reference/pp_decode.md)
runs the package’s combined-oracle stage-1 pipeline (COMP, then GPSR
refinement if needed) on observed pool outcomes; see
[`?pp_decode`](https://myaseen208.github.io/ppgt/reference/pp_decode.md)
and the `ppgt_pp` vignette for the full pipeline. This matrix’s stored
detection limit is:

``` r
attr(M4, "pp")$k_max
  [1] 1
```

so exact COMP recovery is guaranteed only up to 1 true positive out of
282. The example below simulates exactly that many positives with a
fixed seed, so the whole example is reproducible.

``` r
set.seed(20260926)

Y_tilde <- integer(n_specimens)
Y_tilde[137] <- 1L  # the one simulated positive specimen

# Latent pool status: z_tilde_j = 1 iff pool j contains at least one positive
z_tilde <- as.integer(as.vector(M4 %*% Y_tilde) > 0L)
sum(z_tilde)  # number of positive pools
  [1] 4

decoded <- pp_decode(M4, z_tilde, verbose = FALSE)
decoded$positives
  [1] 137
decoded$method
  [1] "COMP (exact)"

stopifnot(identical(decoded$positives, which(Y_tilde == 1L)))
```

[`pp_decode()`](https://myaseen208.github.io/ppgt/reference/pp_decode.md)
recovers the single simulated positive specimen exactly, using only the
4 positive pools out of 188 as evidence.

## 7 Matrix structure

``` r

Matrix::image(
  M4,
  main = "188 x 282 PP pooling matrix (pools x specimens)",
  xlab = "Specimen",
  ylab = "Pool"
)
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Each layer of `nl = 4` contributes a horizontal band of \\q = 47\\
pools; the banded pattern reflects the polynomial-evaluation structure
described in the `ppgt_pp` vignette.
